recentItems.title: Ed McDonald on Bonanno Mafia Member Threatening to Kill Him After His Child Born Disabled (Part 10)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 9: https://youtu.be/FuX5Ca13wjw
Part 1: https://youtu.be/aLB9V7ZJEgc
--------
Former federal prosecutor Ed McDonald sits down with VladTV to discuss the real risks of taking on organized crime in New York City. McDonald explains why prosecutors, FBI agents, and NYPD detectives once believed Mafia figures would not target law enforcement if cases were handled fairly — and why that confidence may have been naive. He recalls a chilling threat from a Sicilian drug dealer tied to the Bonanno crime family, who blamed McDonald after his newborn child was disabled following a conviction. McDonald also details a tense false alarm involving alleged Sicilian Mafia hitmen coming to New York to target anti-mob leaders, with fears reaching his Brooklyn office and even raising questions about Rudy Giuliani’s safety in Manhattan. A revealing look at Mafia prosecutions, law enforcement pressure, and the psychology of the wiseguys facing prison.

recentItems.title: Brian Glaze Gibbs on Crying Over Killing 5 People, Wishing He Could Trade Places with Them (Part 8)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 7: https://youtu.be/a5Y2wARmPtE
Part 1: https://youtu.be/U699JHhcvnM
--------
In this VladTV interview, Brian “Glaze” Gibbs reflects on the painful aftermath of his past violence, breaking down as he discusses the five people he killed and the families forever affected. Speaking with Vlad, Gibbs says he wishes he could trade places with the victims, admitting that chasing power, fear and a “Godfather”-style structure left him with regret instead of fulfillment.

Gibbs opens up about remorse, accountability, losing his mother, and why the gangster image he once embraced is “overrated.” Now living as a law-abiding citizen, husband and taxpayer, he talks about finding peace and using his story to warn rappers and younger generations about crime, ego and consequences. He also shares moments from Martha’s Vineyard, including encounters with Dave Chappelle, Colin Kaepernick, AJ from 106 & Park and John Legend, plus a new health-focused project with Doctor Ronnie.

recentItems.title: Robert O’Neill: I Could Have Killed Bin Laden Easier if I Had Drones (Part 12)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 11: https://youtu.be/Wzs6NWrbUNs
Part 1: https://youtu.be/fA-LpsSTDUs
--------
Robert O’Neill joins Vlad to discuss how the Ukraine war has become a defining test of modern drone warfare, from inexpensive suicide drones to costly countermeasures and the growing role of video-game-trained operators on the battlefield. O’Neill weighs in on Russia, Ukraine funding, trench warfare, robotics, AI, and whether future conflicts will rely less on troops and more on autonomous systems.

The conversation turns to the Osama bin Laden operation, with O’Neill reflecting on how today’s drone technology could have changed the mission. He recalls President Barack Obama’s uncertainty before the raid and explains why confirming bin Laden’s identity still mattered, even with satellite footage and surveillance of the Abbottabad compound courtyard.

From drone swarms and robot soldiers to the possibility of future “robot wars,” O’Neill and Vlad examine how rapidly advancing military tech is reshaping combat in Ukraine and beyond.

recentItems.title: Hit-Boy Signed a F***** Up Deal That Trapped Him for 18-Years: I Felt Like Pooh Shiesty! (Part 14)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 3: https://youtu.be/xmwuD0_g5Ho
Part 1: https://youtu.be/oJzes6G-Jac
--------

Hit-Boy opens up to Vlad and Elliott Wilson about the long-running producer deal he says limited his earnings and leverage for nearly two decades. The Grammy-winning producer details signing as a teenager around Polow Da Don’s circle, working through lawyers tied to Doug Davis, Clive Davis and Jimmy Iovine, and later realizing the impact after producing Jay-Z and Kanye West’s “N****s in Paris.”  

He breaks down how hits with Eminem, Lil Wayne, J.Lo, Flo Rida, Kendrick Lamar, A$AP Rocky and Beyoncé still left him feeling trapped, comparing the frustration to comments around Pooh Shiesty and Gucci Mane. Hit-Boy also reflects on his Interscope imprint, Kanye requesting “Grindin’ My Whole Life,” and the sacrifices behind records like “Clique” and “Theraflu.”  

The conversation expands into music-industry cautionary tales, including Sir Mix-A-Lot, “Baby Got Back,” DJ Punish and publishing ownership.

recentItems.title: 600 Breezy: I Know OTF Jam, If He Was Going to Snitch He Would've Snitched Long Ago (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback clip, we revisit 600 Breezy addressing ongoing street violence and snitching allegations within the hip-hop community. Breezy discussed the tragic death of Lul Pab, which prosecutors have alleged was a case of mistaken identity involving Quando Rondo and his affiliate, Lul Tim. He also addressed speculation that Lil Durk orchestrated retaliatory actions, expressing skepticism due to what he viewed as a lack of evidence. DJ Vlad then questioned OTF Jam’s alleged involvement and whether he could be the person accused of snitching. Breezy firmly defended Jam, pointing to their personal history and Jam’s reputation in the streets while criticizing the tendency to label people as snitches without compelling evidence.
